chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) ruled regarding a free woman, a slave cheated her, so he married her, and she did not know except that he was a free man. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Separation is effected between the two of them if the woman so desires it.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on a free woman marrying a slave who hid his status?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights the principle of *kafa'ah* (compatibility) in Shia jurisprudence, where a slave's status is considered distinct from a free woman's, making the marriage valid but subject to her option of dissolution (*khiyar al-ghurur*). It underscores the legal weight of concealed defects (*'ayb*) in marital contracts, a key topic in *Fiqh al-Sadiq*. The decision reflects the practical application of justice by Ali (AS), prioritizing the woman's consent when material conditions of the marriage were misrepresented.
